prompt:
A line-art multi-panel storyboard of one continuous scene of a live-action short drama: one image divided into a grid of 3 columns and 3 rows of equal 9:16 panels, 8 panels read from left to right and top to bottom; cells after the last panel stay plain white. Every panel is a clean, simple line drawing: uniform thin black outlines on a plain white background, with no shading, hatching, grey tones, colour or texture. Each panel has a thin black border, with plain white gutters between the panels. Location: Jail, a cell, Day, cold flat fluorescent top light with a pale shaft of daylight from the high window.
Image 1: the character sheet of Sebastian (30), look S0
Image 2: the character sheet of Officer (50)
Image 3: the location Jail, a cell, the front view, the establishing view, facing the back wall, with no people
Image 4: the location Jail, a cell, the back view, turned 180 degrees, facing the front wall, with the left wall at its right edge, with no people
Image 5: the location Jail, a cell, the left-side view, facing the left wall, with the back wall at its right edge, with no people
Image 6: the location Jail, a cell, the right-side view, facing the right wall, with the back wall at its left edge, with no people
Image 7: the location Jail, a cell, the floor plan seen from above: its top edge is the back wall, its bottom edge the front wall behind the front view's camera, and its left and right edges the left and right walls, with no people
Image 8: the blocking reference of this segment, the same place with its people in their places at the start; use it only for where each person is and which way they face, and keep each person on that seat or spot, on the same side of the room, in every panel until a shot moves them; do not copy its colours or light
Draw each character so they can be told apart as in their reference image: the hairstyle, build and outfit in outline. Use the character sheets only for the characters, not for their layout, white background or multiple views. Use the location images only for the layout of the space and the place of its furniture and props, drawn in outline. There is only one of each vehicle, piece of furniture and prop that the location shows, defined by the location images, throughout all panels; when a panel shows only part of one, such as a car's hood, it is that same object, and no second one appears. Each panel shows only the characters it names, and nobody appears twice in one panel.
At the start: Camera on the front-wall side of the cell, looking toward the back wall, the steel bunk along the left wall and the barred cell door in the right wall. Sebastian, in the orange prison-issue top and trousers, lies on his side on the thin grey mattress of the one steel bunk along the left wall, his back to the barred cell door, facing the wall, the folded grey blanket at his feet. Officer is walking up the dim corridor outside, toward the barred cell door in the right wall. The one barred high window is in the back wall; the steel toilet-sink unit stands in the back-right corner by the door.
Panel 1: Extreme wide shot, locked-off camera, low angle, establishing insert outside the jail. The blocky grey concrete jail building behind a tall chain-link fence topped with coils of razor wire, under a clear sky.
Panel 2: Wide shot, slow push in, high angle from the front-wall side of the cell. Sebastian lies on the steel bunk along the left wall, his back to the barred cell door, facing the grey-green wall, a shaft of daylight slanting down from the barred high window.
Panel 3: Medium shot, clean single, eye level from the front-wall side, framing the barred cell door. Officer steps up to the barred cell door from the dim corridor, grips a steel bar with one hand and glares toward the bunk.
Panel 4: Medium close-up, clean single, locked-off camera, eye level, framed tight on Sebastian's head and shoulder on the pillow. Sebastian lies facing the wall with his eyes open, calm, and does not turn around; the Officer is off screen.
Panel 5: Close-up, handheld camera, low angle on the Officer through the bars. Officer bangs his key ring hard against the steel bars of the cell door, his face red and furious.
Panel 6: Medium shot, slow pan from the bunk toward the door, eye level from the front-wall side. Sebastian rolls over toward the barred cell door and slowly sits up on the edge of the steel bunk, his feet in the white slip-on canvas shoes on the floor, while the Officer stands at the barred door with his hand on the bars.
Panel 7: Medium close-up, clean single, locked-off camera, eye level, tight on Sebastian's face and shoulders. Sebastian rubs the back of his neck and gives a lazy, amused half-smile toward the door.
Panel 8: Medium shot, over-the-shoulder shot from behind Sebastian's shoulder on the front-wall side, toward the barred door. Officer turns a key in the lock and slides the barred cell door open, then stands in the open doorway frowning at Sebastian on the bunk.
Keep the characters, the number and position of every vehicle, piece of furniture and prop, and the location's spatial orientation consistent across all panels.
No text, letters, numbers, captions, speech bubbles, panel labels or watermark anywhere in the image; no photographic rendering, shading or colour.
